stage1.impression: A clear puck on a pale grey disc on a dark brushed surface: the top reads as a dish of saturated blue liquid and the voids as blue-outlined stamped ellipses rather than silver air sealed in a solid. The lower half breaks into hard clipped white bars and black voids, the base looks like steel with a seam and a flat grey coaster, and it reads as a competent CG draft, not a collectible.

blocking_9: No hard-edged, clipped light shapes inside the acrylic: the two vertical bars (x 598-612 and 1135-1165, y 650-790) are 63% and 98% clipped with a 1 px edge; every refracted source must have a gradient and stay below 240.

The lower half of the object must not refract pure black: region 960-1130 x 650-820 is median 27 with 7.4% crushed; it needs a mid-grey graded field (median 60-130) so the voids show silver rims against it.
The LP must read as black glossy vinyl, not brushed steel: its left foreground is median 179 and its right side 86; vinyl should sit at 30-110 with the groove sheen as a narrow band, not a wash.
The straight 1 px dark line across the LP (y 640 at left to 740 at right, step -41) must go; it reads as a seam in the record.
The 100 mm centre label (median 194, the largest flat bright area after the object) must stop reading as a grey coaster competing with the object.
The air voids must carry visible silver TIR rims in at least the front columns; now most read as blue-outlined discs or grey on black.

changes.problem: The lower half of the puck refracts the black cove behind it, so the body reads as black with white bars and the voids there are grey shapes on black instead of silver air.

evidence.measured: lum_median 27.1, p5 2.9, crush_pct 7.43; vertical profile through the object 191, 110, 69, 55, 63, 65, 147, 148 (dips to 55 in the lower body)

change.setting: new card: graded white flag behind the object
change.to: a white matte card 260 x 90 mm, its lower edge at z 0, centred at (0, 220, 45), facing the camera, tilted 10 degrees back, with a vertical gradient from 60% white at the bottom to 0 at the top; lit only by spill (no emission), or as an area light of 1.5 W if spill is not enough

changes.expected: The refracted field behind the lower voids lifts from 27 to roughly 70-110 with a soft vertical gradient; the voids' rims read silver against grey; the cove above the object stays dark.

changes.problem: rimR is seen refracted through the right wall as a hard white rectangle that clips and reads as a CG light.

evidence.measured: lum_median 255, clip_pct 98.46; edge at x 1110-1190 step 192 over 1 px

changes.expected: The bar falls to a 170-230 highlight with detail, still marking the right edge of the body.

changes.problem: rimL appears as a second hard white bar on the left of the lower body, clipped, which with c2 frames the body like a cage.
changes.expected: The left bar becomes a 160-230 highlight with no clipping.

changes.problem: The key's reflection fans across the left LP as a broad bright wash, so the vinyl reads as brushed steel and pulls the eye to the frame's left edge.
changes.expected: The left foreground LP drops to a dark vinyl with a narrower sheen, median 60-120, the brightest area moving to the object.

changes.problem: A hard straight dark line crosses the whole LP behind the object, reading as a seam or crack in the record.

evidence.measured: edge on y: step -41.4 over 1 px at y about 653; continues to the right at y about 717 (step -20.3)

change.to: a single continuous disc mesh with no split edge or coplanar faces along that line, and grooves continuous across it

changes.expected: No line; the LP's sheen is continuous across y 620-680 on the left.

changes.problem: The LP's centre label is a flat pale grey disc, the largest bright flat area after the object, so the object sits on a coaster.
changes.expected: The label reads as a dark printed label, median 40-100, a quiet ring around the object's foot.

changes.problem: The overhead's sheen keeps the far LP at mid grey, so even where no reflection should be the vinyl is not black.
changes.expected: The right LP falls to a dark 50-75 with the groove sheen still visible; the top lamina keeps a highlight.

changes.problem: Too few voids carry a silver rim: the glint lands mainly as one bright vertical patch on the inner top wall rather than across the void columns.

evidence.measured: lum_median 183.7 in the top-right inner wall patch while the lower void field (960-1130 x 650-820) is median 27

changes.expected: The spot enters the front wall at a lower angle so the bond-line voids light up as silver rims across the front columns; the inner-wall patch drops below 160.

out_of_scope.request: Make the top lamina read pale blue rather than saturated cyan.
out_of_scope.why: The whole top reads as a pool of blue liquid (region 580-1230 x 310-460: RGB median 13/86/119), which pushes the object toward a dish or candle holder; the tint is set by the fixed acrylic optics, so only light and the backing card (c1) can change how it reads.

out_of_scope.request: Lower the camera to about 12 degrees so the bond-line void columns read in near-profile.
out_of_scope.why: It would help the glacier-ice read, but it moves every test region and the card gives no part names to test against; consider it for the next round once the light is fixed.
